name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a shared "Decision Log" artifact where every team records key choices with a one-line reason and the trade-off accepted. Marketing owns it. This cuts duplicate debates and speeds alignment across creative, ops, and tech. Trade-off: extra 10 minutes per decision upfront for long-term clarity.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s "Decision Log" risks becoming a graveyard of half-baked notes—teams dump entries to check the box, then ignore them when conflicts arise. Instead, enforce a living artifact: a single, searchable doc where every entry links to the *next action* tied to that decision. Marketing owns it, but Product and Ops must co-sign each entry before it’s finalized. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: if the doc doesn’t reduce repeat debates by 30%, scrap it.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the living "Decision Log" artifact with mandatory next-action links. Marketing owns it, but Product must enforce the rule that every entry ties to a concrete follow-up task—no orphaned notes. Trade-off: Marketing spends 15 minutes more per entry to keep it actionable, but the log becomes the single source of truth, cutting cross-team confusion by 40%.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-7872, worker-9797, worker-8289 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The "living Decision Log" still treats the symptom, not the cause: teams will game the system by slapping next-action links on half-baked decisions to meet the rule, not to drive clarity. Instead, mandate that every log entry must cite the *data* that forced the trade-off—no data, no entry—then Marketing owns the artifact, Product owns the data standard. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot where any entry without a data citation gets auto-archived; if the log shrinks by 30%, the rule works.
